perf-bot: Automated multi-arch sweep finished: A100 / H100 / L40S. Sweeps: seq=[128,512,2048,8192], bsz=[1,8,32], concurrent=4. Upload: s3://redwood-bench/3801234567/results.json :mag: 
omar: quick summary from eyeballing the CSV: H100 flips kernel at seq=2048 for bsz>=8 -> selects paged-attn fallback; p95 jumps ~2.7x. A100 stays on fused variant until 8192. L40S flips later but shows higher memcpy overhead.
lucy: confirmed on my run: H100 bsz=8 seq=2048 p50=210ms, p95=820ms, tokens/s ~145. When using fused-paged it was ~480 tokens/s for same config on A100.
sasha: interesting — any KV-cache spill observed? I noticed kv-resident size climbs and we see nvlink memcpy spikes on the H100 traces.
omar: yes KV cache resident exceeded GPU bank threshold at the same time as the kernel selector flip. Flamegraph shows big chunk in memcpy and epoll wait (concurrency queues). link: https://internal/fg/3801234567 :eyes: 
natalie: pasted a small snippet of the selector decision log: ```json
{"seq":2048,"bsz":8,"predicted_kernel":"fused_paged","fallback":"paged_attn","reason":"mem_frag+alloc_fail","alloc_bytes":1245189120}```
kevin: "mem_frag+alloc_fail" suggests allocator fragmentation rather than total mem. Were these runs warm or cold? Cold allocs can fragment.
omar: runs were warm (100 iters warmup). We still see occasional spikes on H100 after ~30s, correlates with concurrent streams finishing.
lucy: experiment: reran H100 with single stream (concurrency=1) and prefetch disabled. Selector stayed on fused_paged at seq=2048 and p95 dropped to ~420ms. So concurrency pattern + prefetch seems implicated.
sasha: h100 micro-allocator bug hypothesis: certain memory banks get sticky in mixed precision kernels -> upstream memcpy churn. Can we reproduce with small driver that allocs/frees similar sizes?
omar: plan: 1) run allocator stress microbench (single-gpu) with same alloc patterns 2) run with pinned-allocator toggle 3) add detailed nvprof around memcpy regions. I'll schedule bench job.
natalie: also add a run toggling kernel-selector threshold (increase seq threshold by x1.5) to see perf delta and regression risk. If fused_paged stays enabled we'll need a safe canary.
kevin: for immediate mitigation, we could adjust routing policy to prefer A100 for high-seq, high-bsz as a temporary band-aid for affected customers. Not ideal but buys time.
lucy: FYI L40S showed lower absolute tokens/s but more consistent p95; seems its allocator behavior is less fragmented but memcpy cost higher. Might be different bank layout.
sasha: collating next steps: (a) allocator microbench, (b) nvprof traces, (c) kernel selector threshold tweak, (d) canary routing rule. I'll raise a quick PR for the selector flag.
omar: thanks everyone. tagging @sasha @natalie for follow-up. :thumbsup: If someone can run the allocator microbench today that'd help — otherwise I'll kick it off tomorrow.
perf-bot: Job queued: bench/alloc-stress-3801234567 on h100-1, estimated 2h. Logs: https://ci.redwood/bench/3801234567/logs
